shoal_e20_entry.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_entry.text: On Day Three Hundred Eighty-Nine, the fire-evidence hearing opened in the partnership room under its current accepted public scope. The keeper set chairs far enough apart that nobody had to climb over another person's legs to leave. Outside, ordinary workers continued loading under a different employer. The hearing concerned Shed Six's ignition and current responsibilities. It did not own every loss in the port or offer a single payment large enough to make them disappear.

shoal_e20_hearing_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_hearing_02.text: The clerk read the two dates first. Day Three Hundred One's contained flare had occurred at Shed Three's exterior maintenance table, held by the packing partnership. Its loose oily waste and heat task had been stopped and corrected, with qualified followup on Three Hundred Three. Day Three Hundred Nine's larger fire began inside privately owned Shed Six after a later movement of packing goods. Shared approach lanes did not make the same people responsible for both events.

shoal_e20_hearing_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_hearing_03.text: The qualified maintenance worker who checked Shed Six's lamp bracket on Three Hundred Eight brought the current accepted report. The bracket had met that routine mounting check when inspected. The scope did not promise future trolley positions or a store hand's every movement. He refused an invitation to defend all later work as safe. He had performed a defined ordinary task and could be questioned about that task's actual observations.

shoal_e20_hearing_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_hearing_04.text: The store hand introduced himself as Qiao Deng and asked that he be allowed to finish before people shouted. He had seen the temporary trolley too near the lamp stand. When the cloth slid after its chock shifted, he reached at an angle that struck the stand. The burning oil tipped across loose material. He had shouted the ordinary signal. His account was firsthand about that sequence, including a movement of his own he wanted to undo.

shoal_e20_hearing_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_hearing_05.text: The opposite-side worker, Ai Zhen, had seen the lamp tip and the first flame. She had not seen the chock shift. The clerk asked whether she agreed with Qiao's account. She said it fit what she had seen and included a part she could not personally confirm. That distinction did not weaken her actual view. It prevented two people from becoming one impossible witness who stood at both sides of the store simultaneously.

shoal_e20_hearing_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_hearing_06.text: Yue described the alarm, flame, and crew response visible from her public rope position. Smoke had hidden some later exits. She had not watched the trolley placement, chock, or first hand contact inside. The hearing received her boundary instead of treating a cultivator's presence as omniscience. A listener asked why her practice had not warned her. She said no qualified method she possessed predicted an unobserved future accident.

shoal_e20_hearing_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_hearing_07.text: The private steward, Mao Liu, had arranged the store's current packing assignments. He wanted the hearing to say Qiao alone had caused the fire. Qiao had indeed struck the stand, and the question did not end there. The clerk asked who had authorized the temporary trolley's position and how changed work routes were checked after the routine bracket inspection. Mao's current instruction sheet supplied a separate source to examine.

shoal_e20_hearing_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_hearing_08.text: Mao had told the workers to fit more packing into the cleared room before the next carrier window. He had not instructed them to move a lamp. He had also allowed a changed trolley position without the stated separation being checked by the responsible hand. The ordinary work plan had relied on everyone remembering a safe space while goods moved into it. The hearing needed to distinguish that management decision from Qiao's visible immediate movement.

shoal_e20_hearing_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_hearing_09.text: Qiao said the cloth had been expensive and he had tried to keep it from falling. The owner said cloth could have been replaced more cheaply than a shed. Both statements were true after the event. The clerk asked what workers had actually been instructed to do when loose stock threatened to slide near the lamp. Mao could show no current instruction resolving that specific conflict beyond the ordinary separation rule that the changed arrangement had already violated.

shoal_e20_hearing_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_hearing_10.text: The hearing did not need a hidden arsonist to make the event serious. A shifted chock, nearby stand, loose material, and hurried reach were enough to form a dangerous sequence. The store's ordinary responsibilities included keeping that sequence less likely. Qiao's account remained part of it. The clerk would not turn the absence of a secret enemy into proof that nobody bore responsibility for choices ordinary people could actually change.

shoal_e20_hearing_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_hearing_11.text: A supplier asked whether the early flare had been ignored. The partnership's completed correction record showed the actual exterior task closed, waste secured, and followup performed. The later private store had a different task and a sound bracket check within its limited scope. The hearing would not erase those performed reactions to make a cleaner story of universal negligence. It would ask why the later changed placement had not received its own actual clearance.

shoal_e20_hearing_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_hearing_12.text: Mao said the carrier deadline made the room crowded. The carrier's current contract required safe loading and did not authorize workers to violate the lamp separation. A demanding schedule could create pressure without legally or practically making every dangerous arrangement compulsory. The owner had accepted the deadline and assigned its ordinary staffing. The hearing asked whether a slower safe method had been proposed and who could have refused the changed placement.

shoal_e20_hearing_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_hearing_13.text: Ai described an ordinary objection about the crowded aisle earlier that morning. She had asked for an empty basket moved, and Mao had moved it. The trolley remained where it was because the specific lamp spacing was not checked. Her account showed one real concern answered and another gap left. It did not support a claim that every worker had shouted an ignored fire warning or that Mao had refused every request for space.

shoal_e20_hearing_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_hearing_14.text: The qualified ordinary site examiner identified what could still be observed after the fire and what had been destroyed. Current marks could support the store layout only in limited ways. The examiner used the workers' separate accounts with the surviving instruction sheet and earlier bracket report. She did not claim burnt floor marks could replay the exact arm movement or supply an absent view through smoke.

shoal_e20_hearing_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_hearing_15.text: The hearing chair summarized the supported ignition sequence and held it separate from the provisional responsibility findings. Qiao's reach had tipped the lamp stand. The changed placement and unsecured temporary arrangement had brought loose packing, a lamp, and hurried hands into a preventable conflict. The private owner's delegated steward controlled that work plan. The workers retained responsibility for their own stated actions without becoming substitutes for every organizational decision made above them.

shoal_e20_hearing_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_hearing_16.text: The current material claims would now be received under their owners' actual loss and survival records. What the finite response had preserved changed the stock remaining and the evidence available for each claim. It did not change where the fire had started. Yue checked that the property receiving would use the actual response record, including losses no later careful hearing could reverse.

shoal_e20_property_gate.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_property_gate.text: The property clerk called the owners whose stock had been reachable through the finite safe response. Their current records would establish actual surviving material and irreplaceable loss. Different rescued stock meant different claims and different remaining work capacity. The clerk asked Yue to identify only the receiving she had actually helped perform, leaving each owner to offer its own current evidence.

shoal_e20_drawing_claim_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_drawing_claim_01.text: The drawing owners presented seven fully readable originals and the partial eighth pattern whose five revisions had been lost. Yue confirmed the ordinary receiving of the eight owner-labeled bundles through the long safe route. She did not certify every line of every private drawing. The current owners identified their own sources and losses. Their preserved knowledge had already enabled a narrow later comparison, while the missing revisions still blocked certain claims of complete recovery.

shoal_e20_drawing_claim_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_drawing_claim_02.text: The wooden-form owner had no working forms from the thirty-four lost in the unsafe bay. He supplied his pre-fire inventory under its current consent and the qualified post-fire receiving result. Nine iron bases still had their own ordinary checks and did not become thirty-four surviving wooden forms. The hearing received the loss in that actual form, leaving future replacement costs and business interruptions to their relevant supported claims.

shoal_e20_drawing_claim_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_drawing_claim_03.text: He was angry with Yue for spending her finite response hour on paper. He understood that the qualified crew had selected reachable safe work and was still angry about the consequence. Yue did not tell him the drawings mattered more. She described the ordinary assignment she had accepted and the loss she had seen recorded. His claim against responsible parties did not need her to confess an unsafe rescue she could never have performed.

shoal_e20_drawing_claim_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_drawing_claim_04.text: The drawing owner said preserving her sources had saved part of her business. The form owner said it had not saved his. Both statements remained in the room. The clerk refused to merge them into a single measure of how well the response had gone. Finite crews had limited reach. A lawful useful choice could preserve one owner's means of working and leave another with an irreplaceable practical loss.

shoal_e20_drawing_claim_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_drawing_claim_05.text: The owner's supported claim would include the actually lost forms under the relevant process, with no guarantee that compensation could reproduce their precise old condition. A future replacement would need its own skilled work, materials, and qualified use. The original shop had lost time and particular tools even if money later arrived. Yue kept that distinction when the hearing asked whether the later mechanical review had restored the business.

shoal_e20_drawing_claim_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_drawing_claim_06.text: The review had used a permitted surviving drawing and had not manufactured new original forms. Its report belonged to its own new scope. The property clerk recorded that fact, then returned to the fire loss evidence. A useful later adaptation was not an owner payment received from this hearing. The form owner's current claim remained valid where supported, and the drawing owners retained their source rights rather than surrendering them as the price of recognition.

shoal_e20_drawing_claim_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_drawing_claim_07.text: One listener said the long-route paper rescue had been too cautious. Yan Su described the protection line and the unsafe approaches the qualified crew had rejected. He had not had unlimited crews, time, or safe access to every bay. An observer could regret the lost forms without proposing that heat should have obeyed bravery. Yue's quarter-unit marker task could not have crossed the burning bay and carried thirty-four forms out.

shoal_e20_drawing_claim_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_drawing_claim_08.text: The clerk closed this material receiving with preserved drawings, partial revisions, lost wooden capacity, and current owner claims kept distinct. Yue's selected response had made a real difference and had not made every other loss disappear. The hearing could now address responsibilities from the actual ignition evidence. It would not rewrite the finite rescue as if the unchosen reachable stock had also survived somewhere outside the room.

shoal_e20_form_claim_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_form_claim_01.text: The form owner presented the qualified current result: twenty-eight ordinarily usable wooden forms, two warped items pending separate adaptation, and four cracked out of service. Yue confirmed her finite assigned water-relay work behind the inspected protection line and its actual early stop when symptoms changed. She had not independently certified the forms. Their owner and qualified readers supplied that evidence, while the crew supplied the containment record.

shoal_e20_form_claim_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_form_claim_02.text: The drawing owners presented the pre-fire inventory of eight annotation bundles and the receiving finding that their original surfaces had burned. They retained any actually existing base copies and ordinary human knowledge, but no lost revision appeared merely because someone remembered part of it. The hearing received that irreplaceable information loss. Current businesses could still work in narrower ways while lacking certain original decisions they could once have verified.

shoal_e20_form_claim_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_form_claim_03.text: One drawing owner was angry with Yue for choosing the relay rather than the long-route receiving group. She knew the current ordinary crews had assigned safe finite roles and remained angry at the material consequence. Yue did not tell her forms mattered more than paper. She described the accepted role and the actual stop. The owner's supported claim did not require a fantasy in which Yue had performed both overlapping assignments.

shoal_e20_form_claim_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_form_claim_04.text: The form owner said the saved stock had preserved actual work capacity. The drawing owner said her missing annotation could not be pressed from a mould. Both statements belonged in the same hearing without one cancelling the other. The clerk rejected a summary declaring every business partly restored in the same way. Finite safe work had saved one kind of resource and allowed a different kind of irreplaceable loss.

shoal_e20_form_claim_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_form_claim_05.text: The drawing owners' relevant claims would include the actually lost originals under the proper process, with no guarantee that compensation could recreate absent revisions. A future redesign would be new skilled work, not a recovered original simply because a similar line could be drawn. Yue kept that distinction when the hearing asked whether the later mechanical review had supplied all the missing technical knowledge.

shoal_e20_form_claim_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_form_claim_06.text: The review had used a permitted surviving form and the present repaired part's actual material record. It had not restored the burned annotation bundles. Its report belonged to a separate new source and qualified ordinary scope. The property clerk recorded that fact before returning to the fire loss. Useful later adaptation was not compensation already received here. The drawing owners retained rights in their remaining actual sources and their supported unfinished claims.

shoal_e20_form_claim_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_form_claim_07.text: One listener praised the relay as proof Yue could safely work through fire. Yan Su corrected the inference. Her task had stayed behind an inspected protection line at ordinary waist height. She had stopped when actual symptoms changed, and an ordinary suitable replacement had continued. No qi shield, medical repair, or unlimited load had protected her. The conditions had made a finite useful role possible; they did not grant her permission to enter a burning bay next time.

shoal_e20_form_claim_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_form_claim_08.text: The clerk closed this material receiving with usable forms, doubtful and rejected pieces, lost annotation surfaces, and current owner claims kept distinct. Yue's selected response had made a real difference and left a different resource gone. The hearing could address responsibility from actual ignition evidence. It would not rewrite the finite rescue as if the unchosen original drawings had also survived somewhere beyond the sources actually presented.

shoal_e20_property_rejoin_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_property_rejoin_01.text: The hearing chair stated a supported ordinary ignition sequence without declaring every responsibility settled by the word accident. The private owner's work plan had allowed a later changed placement inside the lamp separation. Mao Liu had authority over that arrangement and had not checked the relevant clearance. Qiao Deng's reach had tipped the stand. The routine bracket check remained a performed limited check, not a universal guarantee or an excuse for ignoring changed conditions.

shoal_e20_property_rejoin_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_property_rejoin_02.text: The owner's current operating permission would not reopen the burned store through a speech about lessons learned. Any replacement work area needed its ordinary independent setup review, actual staffing, and accepted current terms before use. Mao could be removed or reassigned by his employer under its proper process. The hearing would supply supported findings rather than invent a future dismissal it had no authority to promise.

shoal_e20_property_rejoin_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_property_rejoin_03.text: Qiao asked whether telling the truth meant nobody would employ him again. The chair could not promise every employer's decision. His current responsibility finding would identify his action alongside the organizational arrangement, without labeling him the sole cause of every loss. He had a right to examine the wording and use the proper review process. That mattered, but it did not guarantee that speaking would be painless or profitable.

shoal_e20_property_rejoin_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_property_rejoin_04.text: Ai asked that the final record retain the boundary of her sight. She did not want a later public retelling saying she had seen the chock. The clerk read her proposed wording aloud and received her correction. She accepted the actual statement. A truthful witness could be useful precisely because her account stopped before an uncertain detail. The room did not need to make every person agree on events none of them had all seen.

shoal_e20_property_rejoin_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_property_rejoin_05.text: The owner wanted the exact cloth value noted beside Qiao's motive for reaching. The chair received the offered stock record as part of the current claim and refused an implication that expensive cloth required any dangerous catch. The cloth had a real value. So did ordinary safe work arrangements and the lives inside them. Those values did not become mutually exclusive merely because a hurried movement had connected them badly.

shoal_e20_property_rejoin_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_property_rejoin_06.text: Bo's current supported injury and performed finite care remained separate from whether a private owner owed additional damages under the relevant claim process. The care deposit's actual one hundred twenty had been spent, not held as a reason to declare his remaining loss satisfied. He and Jin could offer their own supported claim through their chosen representative. Neither had to attend a public room and display the leg to make the loss real.

shoal_e20_property_rejoin_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_property_rejoin_07.text: The tool owner who had shoved Yue attended his property receiving under the existing contact boundary and ordinary watch arrangements. His two usable steel tools, one pending sharpening, and three destroyed handles or doubtful metal remained a separate supported loss record. The assault and completed eight-copper clinical restitution did not erase that property claim. Nor did the property loss excuse assaulting a receiving worker who had not caused the fire.

shoal_e20_property_rejoin_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_property_rejoin_08.text: He spoke to the clerk instead of approaching Yue. She remained in her actual witness place and answered only when asked about receiving within her scope. The room did not stage a handshake or require forgiveness as proof that procedures had worked. Distance made both claims easier to hear. He could seek supported property relief while she kept the boundary that had been ordered after the shove.

shoal_e20_property_rejoin_09.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_property_rejoin_09.text: The private owner disputed some replacement values and accepted others for further examination. The hearing did not turn every claimed price into money already paid. Supported losses would go through their actual source and claim process. Some original objects and information could not be reproduced at any ordinary invoice price. The clerk named that limitation instead of using promised compensation to erase the owners' actual present absence.

shoal_e20_property_rejoin_10.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_property_rejoin_10.text: Yan Su answered questions about the ordinary crew response. Known four workers had been brought out through actual reachable routes, and one had suffered a leg fracture. Finite crews had then limited spread and protected chosen accessible material while other stock burned. Their preparation and stops had mattered. No account supported a rescue of every tool, an uninjured ending for every worker, or a cultivation shield holding the sea beyond the quay.

shoal_e20_property_rejoin_11.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_property_rejoin_11.text: A listener wanted the crews called negligent for not reaching the unsafe bay. The qualified command record showed tested approaches, observed heat, actual staffing, and rejected routes. The hearing could examine a specific supported omission if offered. Regret for lost property alone did not establish that an impossible or unsafe entry should have been attempted. The people who had worked there deserved questions rooted in conditions they actually faced.

shoal_e20_property_rejoin_12.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_property_rejoin_12.text: Another listener wanted all crew decisions beyond question because they had been brave. Yan declined that protection too. A current decision could be examined from its actual information and limits. Respect for crews did not require pretending every later criticism was disloyal. The chair kept the review narrow enough to hear a supported concern and firm enough to refuse an invented route through heat that nobody had safely entered.

shoal_e20_property_rejoin_13.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_property_rejoin_13.text: By the closing interval, the room had supported findings, current responsibilities, and unfinished loss claims. It had no universal villain and no universal absolution. Mao left with the owner's representative, both silent enough that Yue could not read their future conversation. Qiao stayed to correct one ordinary spelling in his name. Ai asked where the permitted final copy would be available. People returned to individual lives larger than their places in a fire account.

shoal_e20_property_rejoin_14.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_property_rejoin_14.text: The final public notice would summarize the supported ignition and the separate continuing claims. It would identify the early contained exterior flare as a different event and record the actual later changed arrangement. The clerk invited an ordinary two-hour assistant interval for arranging its permitted public copy before the next board posting. Yue could help if she accepted, but the work would not reopen her finished witness role indefinitely.

shoal_e20_property_rejoin_15.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_property_rejoin_15.text: Qiao separately asked whether Yue would walk a short public route with him after the hearing. He wanted a conversation with someone who had heard the findings and was not his employer. He did not ask her to certify innocence or erase his own action. The same offered interval was all she had before the next ordinary commitment. The clerk could post later if the copy helper declined; Qiao might leave for a current family visit before another talk fit.

shoal_e20_property_rejoin_16.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_property_rejoin_16.text: Yue asked Qiao whether he had suitable people to speak with if she chose the notice. He had relatives and could use existing ordinary support routes. He still wanted this particular offered conversation. The clerk said the public notice's present posting deadline would pass without the extra organizing help, and a later posting would need its own actual interval. Both offers had bounded useful consequences, with no clinical treatment waiting on Yue's answer.

shoal_e20_property_rejoin_17.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_property_rejoin_17.text: The decision was easier to name than to make. A careful public summary could prevent another wave of false certainty about the fire. A private ordinary walk could let a frightened worker speak beyond the line where his testimony stopped. Neither action would change the actual ignition sequence. Both could change what happened afterward to people who would keep living with it. Yue could choose one and let the other need a later road.

shoal_e20_property_rejoin_18.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_property_rejoin_18.text: She had no paid review shift on this hearing day. The new appointment's next week began on Three Hundred Ninety-One, and today's offered assistance belonged outside its wage source. Qiao's family visit and the public posting each had actual current times. Yue kept her ordinary walking limits in mind. She would not turn the walk into care beyond her role or the notice into a promise that every listener would believe it.

shoal_e20_aftermath_choice.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_aftermath_choice.text: After the hearing, one offered interval remained. The clerk wanted help arranging the permitted accurate public summary before its posting deadline. Qiao wanted an ordinary public walk before leaving on a family visit, with no request for innocence or medical care. The unchosen offer would miss its present hour. Yue chose which useful work after truth-telling she wished to fulfill.

choices.text: Help post the supported public summary on its current date.
Walk with Qiao and hear the ordinary person beyond his testimony.

shoal_e20_notice_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_notice_01.text: Yue sat at the public copy table with the clerk and the final accepted text. The first draft's opening placed the early flare and later fire in one sentence that could imply a shared cause. She asked for the dates and locations in separate ordinary clauses. The clerk agreed because the supported record required the distinction. The new copy made the actual relation clearer without removing either event to make the town look safer.

shoal_e20_notice_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_notice_02.text: They kept Qiao's immediate action in the summary and the owner's changed work arrangement beside it. A short notice could not carry every private claim. It could carry enough actual structure to prevent a single named worker becoming the convenient explanation for every destroyed business. The clerk checked the wording against the accepted findings and asked the authorized receiver to approve the current public version.

shoal_e20_notice_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_notice_03.text: Ai's actual view remained separate from Qiao's. Yue noticed that a copied phrase had accidentally made both witnesses see the shifted chock. The clerk corrected it before posting and returned to the source. The error was small, meaningful, and now removed from this copy. The clerk kept the mistaken copy until she had checked the correction, then marked it discarded. Yue read the new line again before handing it back.

shoal_e20_notice_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_notice_04.text: The authorized receiver accepted the corrected public copy. It reached the board before the current posting deadline, with its continuing claim routes and proper source contact. People reading it would still disagree about responsibility. They would have a more accurate common account to dispute. Yue received no new wage for the offered two hours and claimed no new authority because her handwriting appeared beneath the clerk's approved text.

shoal_e20_notice_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_notice_05.text: Qiao's current family departure occurred without the offered walk. He traveled through his own accepted arrangements and could speak to his relatives if he chose. The conversation he wanted with Yue remained missed. A public notice that treated his action fairly did not substitute for an hour when he could have been a person beyond that action. He sent no message asking her to pretend it did.

shoal_e20_notice_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_notice_06.text: At the board, a supplier read the notice and objected that it sounded complicated. The clerk said the supported event involved several ordinary decisions and different actual witnesses. Complexity was not permission to invent a simpler false version. The supplier could challenge a specific line through the stated process. He took the contact details instead of demanding that Yue decide the hearing again on the public lane.

shoal_e20_notice_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_notice_07.text: A worker asked whether the notice meant everyone would receive compensation. Yue pointed to the actual continuing claim language and its limits. The current public summary had not received every claimed payment. The worker was disappointed and copied the proper request address. Useful information could leave a person needing more work. Yue did not turn his disappointment into an argument that the notice should never have been posted.

shoal_e20_notice_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_notice_08.text: The clerk closed the copying interval at its promised hour. Yue returned the temporary source extract and left the posted copy with its proper receiving authority. She had chosen a public consequence that made the supported findings available sooner. Qiao's missed walk remained a private consequence she could not inspect from the board. Her useful two hours did not become a claim on every reader's future understanding.

shoal_e20_walk_01.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_walk_01.text: Qiao met Yue at the public door and chose a short route clear of the closed store boundary. He carried a small bag for his family visit. The walk did not make him her patient or her responsibility beyond the offered hour. For a while he spoke only about the bag's broken button and a cousin who always overfilled tea cups. Yue let the ordinary subjects stand instead of dragging him back to the lamp.

shoal_e20_walk_02.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_walk_02.text: He finally said he could replay the reach whenever he shut his eyes. He knew the cloth could have fallen and that the knowledge had arrived too late to change his hand. Yue said she could hear him without knowing how every night would feel afterward. She did not prescribe a remedy or claim her own bruise matched his fear. Existing qualified support could be approached through his actual ordinary routes if he wanted it.

shoal_e20_walk_03.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_walk_03.text: Qiao was worried his mother would ask whether he had caused the whole fire. Yue described the supported finding's distinction between his immediate movement and the changed work arrangement. It was not a sentence declaring him blameless. It was an account that let his actual action sit among other actual decisions. He said he needed to learn how to tell it without sounding as though he was hiding behind the steward.

shoal_e20_walk_04.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_walk_04.text: They stopped at a public stall where each paid for an ordinary cup within personal means. Qiao did not ask Yue to pay for him because she had come. He talked about the last time he had visited home and discovered his younger sister had grown tall enough to look unimpressed by him. He hoped she would do it again. Fear had left room for an ordinary wish unrelated to the hearing's final page.

shoal_e20_walk_05.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_walk_05.text: At the public copy table, the extra organizing interval remained unfilled. The clerk completed its existing assigned work and arranged the accurate summary for a later accepted posting hour. Today's board deadline passed. The supported findings still existed in their proper record, but more people would spend another interval relying on incomplete retellings. Qiao's useful walk had not made the public copy secretly finish in his absence.

shoal_e20_walk_06.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_walk_06.text: Yue heard that result before the offered hour ended. Qiao said perhaps she should have gone to the notice. She answered that she had chosen the walk and would not make him repay it by calling his request less worthwhile. The later public posting would be actual new work. They could acknowledge its cost without deciding that his ordinary conversation had been stolen from a town that needed information.

shoal_e20_walk_07.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_walk_07.text: At the carrier door, Qiao checked his actual family departure with the receiving clerk. Yue did not accompany him past the permitted public point. He thanked her for an hour when he had spoken about his sister and not only the fire. The thanks did not certify his future well-being. It named a real offered conversation, completed before his booked journey took him to people whose questions he would answer himself.

shoal_e20_walk_08.speaker: narrator
shoal_e20_walk_08.text: Yue returned by the longer ordinary lane. The board still lacked its new summary at the missed current deadline. She had heard a person she might otherwise have remembered only as a hand beside a lamp. The gain and the public delay both remained. She did not use one to excuse inventing the other.
